thread.title_full: Two 'doomsday fish' wash up on Mexico beach and it's causing panic - NewsBreak

author: Parul Sharma
title: Two 'doomsday fish' wash up on Mexico beach and it's causing panic - NewsBreak
text:
By Parul Sharma ,
44 minutes ago In a startling discovery on the shores of Cabo San Lucas in Mexico, two exceptionally rare deep-sea creatures, commonly referred to as 'doomsday fish', were found struggling on the sand, far from their usual habitat.
Ancient folklore suggests that the seldom-seen deep-sea oarfish serves as an omen of impending disaster, and the simultaneous appearance of two such specimens could signal something truly catastrophic on the horizon.
• Psychic who predicted Covid claims Jeffrey Epstein bombshell coming this summer
• 'I am a psychic and America will take over Cuba and Greenland this year'
These elongated, ribbon-shaped fish are mysterious deep-sea dwellers, typically inhabiting depths of 1,000 meters (3,280 feet) and rarely venturing near the surface - making the dual appearance of these uncommon oarfish an exceptionally peculiar and remarkable occurrence.
The rare encounter Beach visitor Monica Pittenger, working with the account We Love Animals, initially shared the startling video footage of the incident on Instagram on March 4, 2026, capturing the two deep-sea fish writhing on the shoreline, reports the Mirror .
In the footage, the oarfish are visible stranded on the Mexican coastline, with one of the unfortunate creatures desperately thrashing about out of water. The camera then shifts to reveal a second oarfish, similarly trapped in the liminal space between ocean and land.
Onlookers gradually begin congregating around the first doomsday fish, and one woman in the footage (subsequently identified by Monica as her sister Katie) can be observed crouching down as she attempts to guide the creature back toward the sea. Moments later, additional bystanders arrived on the scene and collectively worked to guide the deep-sea oarfish back into the ocean.
In the footage, Monica can be heard saying: "I didn't believe my eyes. It was like something out of a fiction movie. I had never seen anything like it before. I just remember thinking, is this real?! And honestly, when I saw the second one, I got a little nervous."
Monica described how she and her companions "saw something in the distance" and noted "It was flashing, and it was really bright."
She added: "And when we saw them up close, it was like nothing we've seen before, so we were like, 'This can't be real.'"
Monica revealed how her sister Katie "just cannot stand anything in pain" and responded to the distressing scene "super fast" to assist the creature in returning to the water. Katie received immediate support from a young girl, with more volunteers eventually stepping in to aid the rescue effort.
Monica recalled: "Just watching all these men standing around, and she [Katie] throws me her phone and her drink and her bag, and she's like, 'Hold this.'"
"I think a lot of people were very hesitant because nobody really knew what it was. It's not every day that you see that. And I mean, I don't blame them."
After successfully returning the first oarfish to the sea, the spontaneous rescue team reportedly made their way to the second fish, which Katie and the group also helped guide back into the water.
Speculation that the video was AI-generated spread rapidly (as tends to happen these days), but Monica put those doubts to rest in a comment beneath her original Instagram post, responding to skeptics questioning its authenticity: "It's not AI!! It's my video."
Why the sighting is sparking alarm Oarfish can reach lengths of up to 30 feet, and according to Japanese folklore, these deep-sea dwellers are dispatched as messengers from the sea gods to warn of approaching catastrophe in the form of natural disasters like tsunamis and earthquakes.
Whilst the mesopelagic-dwelling creatures have been associated with tsunamis and earthquakes in mythology for centuries, scientists have discovered no concrete evidence that their appearance, however uncommon, can forecast natural disasters. According to Surfer, no seismic events have occurred following this 'doomsday fish' sighting so far.
The massive fish's notoriety as a harbinger of misfortune overshadows its genuinely harmless disposition, having been employed as an indicator to forecast real-world natural calamities and devastating disasters.
The internet has, understandably, gone into meltdown over the sighting, with one X user posting: "The ocean drops two literal harbingers of doom on the beach at Cabo, is it time to rethink that trip or just bring my doomsday kit and pretend everything is fine?"
Another social media user commented: "Seeing the 'doomsday fish' on the surface is always a chilling sight. Whether it's seismic activity or shifting ocean currents, something deep down is definitely changing. Nature is sending us a signal we shouldn't ignore."
Meanwhile, one X user said: "Two doomsday fish washing up in quick succession may be telling us something. Especially when only a few have ever washed up over several hundred years."
Another user cheekily wrote: "Two 20–30 ft oarfish basically doing a surprise beach cameo in Cabo? That's not just rare , it's statistically absurd. Normally they chill at 3,000 ft deep where it's pitch black and zero drama. People pushing them back into the water like it's a group project is wholesome chaos."
summary: 20 minutes ago In a startling discovery on the shores of Cabo San Lucas in Mexico, two exceptionally rare deep-sea creatures, commonly referred to as 'doomsday fish', were found struggling on the sand, far from their usual habitat. The rare encounter Beach visitor Monica Pittenger, working with the account We Love Animals, initially shared the startling video footage of the incident on Instagram on March 4, 2026, capturing the two deep-sea fish writhing on the shoreline, reports the Mirror .
